opus-5.5.text:
I think of them as two halves of the same goal rather than two separate product lines.

Pro is where we push the ceiling on reasoning: long-horizon thinking, coding, agentic tasks, the ability to plan, check its own work, and recover from mistakes. Omni is about perception and interaction: seeing, hearing, speaking, operating in real environments, and responding in real time. For a long time people treated these as a tradeoff, a smart but slow text model on one side and a fast multimodal model on the other. I don't think that split is sustainable.

What I hope to see is the two feeding each other. The reasoning ability we build in Pro should flow into Omni, so that when it looks at a screen, a video, or a physical scene, it isn't just describing what's there but actually thinking about it: what's going on, what to do next, what could go wrong. In the other direction, Omni gives Pro something it badly needs, which is grounding. A pure text model reasons over a compressed, secondhand version of the world. Once you add vision, audio, and interaction, you get much richer feedback signals, and those signals become new training data and new environments for reinforcement learning. That's how reasoning stops being purely symbolic and becomes connected to reality.

Technically, I believe this converges toward a shared foundation: one backbone, with different inference budgets and interfaces on top. Sometimes you want it to think for minutes, sometimes you want it to answer in two hundred milliseconds while you're talking to it. The ideal system can move along that spectrum on its own and decide when to think deeply and when to just respond.

So in the short term they'll keep their different emphases, because the engineering constraints really are different. In the long run, though, I don't think users should have to choose between a model that's smart and a model that can see and talk. The end state is a single intelligence that is both.

r001.rationale: The response says the two should feed each other: Pro’s reasoning should flow into Omni, while Omni’s grounding and feedback should improve Pro.

fable-5.1.text:
I think the honest answer is that they're not two separate roadmaps that happen to live in the same building. They're really one project seen from two angles.

Pro is where we push the ceiling on reasoning, on coding, on long-horizon agent behavior. Omni is where we push the model to actually perceive the world: speech, vision, video, all the messy signals that don't arrive as clean text. For a long time the industry treated those as different problems with different teams and different training recipes. What we've found is that the two keep feeding each other.

Concretely, almost everything Pro learns about reasoning transfers into Omni. If the base model is better at planning and self-correction, then when you put a camera and a microphone in front of it, it makes better use of what it sees and hears. It doesn't just describe the scene, it understands why the scene matters for the task. On the other side, Omni teaches us things about data and grounding that Pro alone would never surface. Text is a lossy compression of the world. When you train on real audio and video, you encounter all the ambiguity and timing and context that text quietly drops, and that forces you to build more robust representations. Those improvements flow back into the text model.

So the way I picture it is a kind of shared backbone that keeps getting stronger, with Pro and Omni as two expressions of it. Over the next few generations I expect the gap between them to narrow. The ideal state is that you don't ask "do I want the smart one or the one that can see" — the model is smart because it can see and hear, and it sees and hears well because it's smart.

And for Xiaomi specifically, that matters a lot. We have phones, cars, home devices, hundreds of millions of endpoints that are constantly perceiving. A model that can only reason in text is a brilliant assistant stuck behind a keyboard. A model that perceives but can't reason deeply is a very good sensor. We want the thing in the middle, and Omni and Pro growing together is how we get there.

r001.rationale: The response says Pro’s reasoning improvements transfer into Omni, while Omni’s data and grounding improvements flow back into Pro, and describes them as growing together.

astra-6.text: I see Omni and Pro improving through a shared feedback loop. Pro can strengthen reasoning and reliability, while Omni can make interactions more natural across different kinds of input and output. The opportunity is to bring those strengths together: richer interaction should help the model understand what someone needs, and stronger reasoning should help it respond more usefully. I’d want progress in either one to benefit the other, so users experience a more capable, coherent system.

r001.rationale: The response describes a shared feedback loop and says progress in either Omni or Pro should benefit the other.

sol-6.1.text: I see Omni and Pro improving in a complementary way. Pro can push the depth of reasoning and problem-solving, while Omni can make those capabilities more natural to use across different kinds of input and interaction. The goal is for them to reinforce each other, so users can move fluidly between a natural conversation and a task that requires deeper thought. Better intelligence should make the interaction more useful, and better interaction should make that intelligence more accessible.

r001.rationale: It says Omni and Pro should “reinforce each other,” describing complementary contributions to their improvement.
